debate_title: Mandatory pre-deployment safety evaluations for frontier ...

conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment evaluation mandates effectively contain frontier AI risks or merely drive open-source development underground while failing to stop malicious actors.

positions.stance: Mandatory pre-deployment checks impose prohibitive legal and administrative costs on independent developers while failing to prevent the proliferation of dual-use models.
Pre-deployment evaluations provide an essential regulatory gate that prevents unverified, potentially irreversible capabilities from reaching public distribution.

conflicts.point: Whether digital model weights can be effectively recalled or contained post-release, or if governance must rely primarily on runtime monitoring and post-deployment auditing.

positions.stance: Open-weight distribution coupled with decentralized runtime isolation and continuous auditing is more effective at mitigating misuse than static pre-release gating.
Once model weights are distributed publicly, they cannot be recalled, making pre-release containment the only viable point of intervention for irreversible risks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment evaluation mandates effectively contain frontier AI risks or merely drive open-source development underground while failing to stop malicious actors.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position accounts for irreversible catastrophic outcomes that bypass standard market corrections, whereas the accelerationist critique relies on unproven assumptions about underground enforcement evasion. Pre-deployment gates establish a necessary baseline verification before public release occurs.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical evidence showing that malicious actors routinely bypass pre-deployment controls while legitimate open-source developers suffer catastrophic compliance failures would flip this verdict.

verdicts.conflict: Whether digital model weights can be effectively recalled or contained post-release, or if governance must rely primarily on runtime monitoring and post-deployment auditing.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist argument correctly identifies the irreversible nature of public weight distribution, whereas the accelerationist analogy to runtime monitoring lacks a mechanism to recall already downloaded weights. Once code is copied globally, preventative containment remains the only logically sound intervention point.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: The development of cryptographic or hardware-enforced revocation mechanisms that can reliably delete or disable open-weights post-release would invalidate the permanence claim.
